_what: Which command advances which stage. next_commands.py reads it.
_why: automaton.py --next knows WHICH unit is actionable and has never been able to say WHAT to run, because nothing recorded the mapping. This records it. Edit it when a tool changes - it is data, not code.
_honesty: cmd:null means nobody has confirmed the command. The candidates are listed so the next person can confirm one instead of guessing. Every command below uses only flags printed by that script's own --help on 2026-09-14.

ocr.note: Four plausible entry points and no way to tell them apart from flags alone. Confirm one before the driver is allowed to run this stage.

ingest.note: Pass the category explicitly. The tool's own hint is hardcoded from the document it was written for.

segment.note: SUPERVISED. This writes JSONL only, and is only step one of five: ingest the JSONL, diag_retire_check, graft if it refuses, retire. Run it through block_AR_phase2.ps1, which has the gates. driver:false because a loop handed this command would re-segment an already-segmented document into {code}_seg_seg - which is exactly what the first draft of next_commands.py did on a fixture.

classify.note: Three scripts, probably three different jobs rather than three ways to do one.

iast.note: There is no iast runner and there does not need to be: ingest_jsonl_fast.py takes --no-iast, so IAST is produced at ingest unless suppressed. A document short of IAST was ingested with it off, or ingested before the feature existed. Re-ingest is the fix, not a new tool.

translate_en.note: engine string observed in a live run on 2026-09-14.

translate_hi.note: Same tool as English. translate_hi was never a separate script. Hindi lands in translations_l10n at lang='hi'; English lands in passages.translation.

qa.note: qa_report reads, heal_lowqa writes, qa_scan is ambiguous. Confirm before wiring.

entities.note: --batch, --limit, --sleep and --retry-empty exist. --retry-empty is what made the maintenance runner exceed PT1H in September; leave it off in a driver.

embed.note: --model and --list-models exist; the default is used here rather than pinning a model I have not seen.

morph.note: THE FLAG. ling_kosha.py takes both --survey and --commit. 50.1% coverage was measured in September and 0 rows were ever written, across 48,823 live passages. Everything ever run against it was a survey.

export.note: export_mb01_html.py and export_mb01_md.py are document-specific and are not general answers.

book.note: One candidate, but its flags were not read. 37 documents are READY for this stage, which makes it the cheapest large win in the corpus once the command is confirmed.
